requests.administrative_note: Only explicitly listed interrupted-pair attempt IDs are excluded from primary code workflows; their raw terminal calls and unknown-usage journal starts remain in all-attempt accounting. Administrative collector interruptions are not provider failures. Gateway status/duration never substitute for missing client protocol, latency or usage.
requests.cost_note: Usage-based USD list-equivalent estimate only, not exact billing or subscription deductions. Request start in Asia/Shanghai selects weekday peak 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–18:00, else off-peak. Per-million input/cache/output: peak 0.30/0.006/1.20, off 0.15/0.003/0.60. Prompt tokens include cached tokens: subtract cache before uncached rate. Completion tokens already include reasoning; never add reasoning a second time. Missing usage/cache/time leaves estimate unknown. Unreturned/interrupted usage can remain unknown.
requests.observed_concurrency_note: Timestamp reconstruction uses all recorded terminal calls across phases. It is a lower bound whenever in-flight/administratively interrupted calls lack client terminal times. Nominal concurrency_per_provider is runner metadata, not proof of total simultaneous link/provider load. Half-open intervals exclude calls ending exactly when another begins. Collector recovery metadata, not apparent journal overlap alone, determines administrative interpretation.
requests.workflow_accounting_note: Workflow throughput uses runner-recorded chosen first/repair or episode responses. Every terminal attempt remains in request totals. Requests not yet referenced by terminal workflows are separately listed; pending or abandoned state and any additional overhead require review, not automatic deletion.

Auto-strip alternative, if selected, is posthoc and deterministic; it does not change actual measured wait.
